items.title: Topic Three's Verses Close: Pride's Final Extinction, and Craving's Five Causes

items.zh: 又即於此多修習故，永斷三界修斷我慢。由此斷故，說名無學離三界欲，上下貪斷，已得安隱。一切苦因皆捨離故，證得一切眾苦邊際。
items.en: And by extensively cultivating this same signless concentration, one permanently severs the pride belonging to the path of cultivation across all three realms. By this severing, one is called "beyond training," free of desire for all three realms, both lower and higher craving cut off, having attained genuine peace. Because every cause of suffering has been abandoned entirely, one realises the very limit of all suffering.

items.zh: 如是故言：修習於無相，壞慢及隨眠；由於慢現觀，當證苦邊際。
items.en: Therefore it is said: 'Cultivating the signless, one destroys conceit and its latent tendency; through direct realisation of conceit, one will realise the end of suffering.'

items.zh: 復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂顯貪欲，由是而生，由是寂靜及彼寂靜，當知是名此中略義。云何貪欲由是而生？謂五因故。一、由淨妙想，二、由欣樂樂，三、由有情想，四、由猛盛貪，五、由隨眠有餘未盡。
items.en: Further, let what has been said above now be briefly explained. It shows how craving-desire arises, and how it is stilled, and its stillness fully realised — know this to be the brief explanation given here. How does craving-desire arise? From five causes: first, from perceiving something as pure and lovely; second, from delight taken in that perception; third, from conceiving of a being as such; fourth, from craving already intensely habituated; and fifth, from the latent tendency not yet entirely exhausted.

items.title: Topic Three Closes: Five Causes of Stillness, and Two Depths of Freedom

items.zh: 云何貪欲生已，由是寂靜？謂五因故。一、由作意思惟不淨，二、由作意思惟於苦，三、由作意思惟無我，四、由繫念多修厭離，五、由隨眠無餘永滅。
items.en: How, once craving-desire has arisen, is it stilled? From five causes: first, from applying the mind to reflect on impurity; second, from applying the mind to reflect on suffering; third, from applying the mind to reflect on non-self; fourth, from sustained mindfulness and extensive cultivation of revulsion; and fifth, from the latent tendency being permanently extinguished without remainder.

items.zh: 云何寂靜？謂此寂靜略有二種。一者、現行寂靜；二者、永斷隨眠，當來不起。由前四種寂靜因緣，成初寂靜；由第五因，第二成就。
items.en: What is stillness? Briefly, this stillness has two kinds: first, stillness of present manifestation; and second, the permanent severance of the latent tendency, such that it never arises again in future. The first four causes accomplish the first kind of stillness; the fifth cause alone accomplishes the second.

items.title: Topic Four Opens: Crossing the Raging Flood

items.zh: 云何苾芻多所住，越五暴流當度六？云何定者能度廣欲愛，而未得腰舟？
items.en: Abiding in what, does a monastic cross the five raging floods, and go on to cross the sixth? How does one who has attained concentration, having already crossed the vast flood of craving, still lack the "waist-float" that would carry them the rest of the way?

items.zh: 身輕安、心善解脫、無作、繫念、不傾動、了法、修習無尋定、憤愛惛沈過解脫。如是苾芻多所住，越五暴流當度六。如是定者能度廣欲愛而未得腰舟。
items.en: With body at ease and mind well liberated, mindfulness unmoving, engaged in no contrivance; understanding the Dharma, cultivating concentration free of examination, one is liberated from the faults of rage, craving, and torpor. Abiding thus, a monastic crosses the five raging floods, and goes on to cross the sixth; thus does one who has attained concentration cross the vast craving of desire, though not yet having attained the "waist-float."
This verse arose from a question asked by a goddess.

items.title: Crossing the Five Floods: Bodily Ease and the Six Senses

items.zh: 暴流有六。謂眼暴流能見諸色，乃至意暴流能了諸法。
items.en: There are six floods: the flood of the eye, by which forms are seen, and so on through to the flood of the mind, by which mental objects are cognized.

items.zh: 佛聖弟子有學見迹、於隨順喜眼所識色，不住於愛；於隨順憂眼所識色，不住於恚；於隨順捨眼所識色，數數思擇，安住於捨。
items.en: The Buddha's noble disciples, having entered the path as trainees, do not dwell in craving towards forms seen by the eye that incline towards pleasure; do not dwell in aversion towards forms seen by the eye that incline towards displeasure; and, towards forms seen by the eye that incline towards neutrality, repeatedly discern them well and abide in equanimity.

items.zh: 彼設已生或欲貪纏、或瞋恚纏、或愚癡纏，三身為緣，所謂喜身、憂身、捨身；而不堅著乃至變吐。由是因緣，於屬三身諸煩惱纏得不現行，輕安而住。如是名為得身輕安，而未能得心善解脫。由彼隨眠未永斷故。
items.en: Should craving, aversion, or delusion nonetheless arise, resting on these three conditions — the accumulated body of pleasure, of displeasure, or of neutrality — they do not cling to it firmly, and it is discarded, even purged entirely. By this cause, the afflictions belonging to these three bodies fail to manifest, and one dwells at ease. This is called attaining bodily ease — though the mind is not yet fully liberated, since the underlying latent tendency has not yet been permanently severed.

items.title: Crossing the Sixth Flood: No Contrivance, No Movement, Sustained Mindfulness

items.zh: 彼於後時，又能永斷屬彼隨眠，即於屬彼諸煩惱中遠離隨縛。如是乃名即於三身貪瞋癡所心善解脫。如於眼所識色，乃至於身所識觸，當知亦爾。如是已斷五下分結，越五暴流。
items.en: Continuing afterwards, one becomes able to permanently sever the latent tendency belonging to these afflictions, becoming free of their binding entirely. Only this is called being genuinely well liberated in mind from the craving, aversion, and delusion belonging to these three bodies. Thus, having severed the five lower fetters, the five floods are crossed.

items.zh: 謂越眼暴流能見諸色，乃至越身暴流能覺諸觸。
items.en: That is, crossing the flood of the eye, one can see forms; and so on through crossing the flood of the body, one can feel tangibles.

items.zh: 如是越度五暴流已，餘有第六意暴流在。為當越度，復修無作、無動、繫念。云何無作？謂於涅槃心生願樂，不為我慢之所傾動；無所思惟，亦無造作。又不為彼計我我所當來是有，乃至我當非想非非想等之所傾動；無所思惟，亦無造作。
items.en: Having thus crossed the five floods, the sixth flood, the flood of mind, still remains. To cross it as well, one further cultivates no contrivance, no movement, and sustained mindfulness. What is no contrivance? It means that, the mind having grown to delight in nirvāṇa, one is no longer moved by pride, and there is nothing to deliberate over, nothing to construct. Nor is one moved by conceiving a self or what is mine as existing in the future, down to conceiving "I shall become neither perceiving nor non-perceiving" — there is nothing to deliberate over, nothing to construct.

items.zh: 云何無動？謂不為彼上分諸結纏繞其心。無動無變，亦無改轉。又於隨一寂靜諸定，不生愛味、戀慕、堅著。
items.en: What is no movement? It means the mind is no longer entangled by any of the higher fetters — unmoved, unchanged, undiverted. And towards any of the peaceful meditative absorptions, no delight, longing, or firm attachment arises.

items.title: Sustained Mindfulness Completes the Sixth Flood, and Loving-Kindness as a Second Path

items.zh: 云何繫念？謂為斷彼上分諸結，於其內身住循身觀，如是乃至廣說念住。彼由如是修無作故，斷諸生愛；修無動故，斷諸定愛。此離現行，說名為斷。修繫念故，為令一切上分諸結無餘永斷，修習對治。
items.en: What is sustained mindfulness? It means that, in order to sever the higher fetters, one abides observing the body within the body, and so on through the remaining foundations of mindfulness in full. By cultivating no contrivance in this way, one severs craving for further existence; by cultivating no movement, one severs craving for meditative absorption itself. This is freedom from present manifestation, called "severing." By cultivating sustained mindfulness, one applies the actual antidote that permanently severs every higher fetter without remainder.

items.zh: 如是修習無作、繫念、不傾動故，能令一切上分諸結無餘永斷。是名越度第六暴流。謂意暴流能了諸法。復有差別。云何無動？
items.en: Because one cultivates in this way, without contrivance, with mindfulness fixed and unshaken, one can cut off all the higher fetters for ever without remainder. This is called crossing the sixth flood, the flood of the mind, which cognises dharmas. There is a further distinction. What is unshaken?

items.zh: 言無動者，是慈善根，無瞋性故。由此因緣，諸聖弟子於薩迦耶斷除邪願，修奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。由彼慈故，修奢摩他；由念住故、修毘鉢舍那。
items.en: "No movement," under a second explanation, is the wholesome root of loving-kindness, being by nature free of hatred. By this cause, the noble disciples abandon misguided aspiration regarding the perishable-body view, cultivating both calm-abiding and insight — calm-abiding through loving-kindness, insight through the foundations of mindfulness.

items.zh: 如是正修行者，於能隨順斷上分結三心修習，速得圓滿。謂於上身無耽染心；於下有情無憤恚心；不放逸者，於上下境無染污心。餘如前說。如是名為越五暴流，當度第六。
items.en: One who thus rightly practices swiftly perfects the three states of mind that accord with severing the higher fetters: no attachment towards higher forms of existence, no hostility towards lower beings, and — free of heedlessness — no defiled mind towards objects high or low. This is called crossing the five floods, and going on to cross the sixth.

blocks.text: Two topics today. First, the close of the teaching on a mind burning with desire: why craving arises, and how it is stilled. Then a goddess asks how a monk crosses the "floods" and the "vast craving". Several explanatory questions and short summaries are missing from the English.

"Cultivate the signless, destroying pride and its latent tendency." What remains after seeing the truths is the pride of the path of cultivation. Venerable Miào Jìng: a stream-enterer already senses non-self, "but pride remains: 'you haven't practised, I have'". Only its complete removal makes one "beyond training".

subs.head: Five causes of craving, five of stillness

blocks.text: Craving arises (1) from perceiving something as lovely, (2) from delight in that perception, (3) from conceiving a being as such (Venerable Miào Jìng: "because you make the distinction of male and female"), (4) from deeply habituated craving, and (5) from the latent tendency.

It is stilled (1) by reflecting on impurity, (2) on suffering, (3) on non-self, (4) by sustained mindfulness and revulsion, and (5) by the tendency's final extinction. The first four bring **stillness of manifestation**; only the fifth brings **permanent severance**. Master Cháng Bǎi: a seed is "the functional capacity that can produce phenomena"; craving that does not show is not therefore gone.

A goddess asks: abiding in what does a monk cross five floods and then the sixth? How does one in concentration cross the vast craving, yet lack the "waist-float"? Venerable Miào Jìng: a slow stream is easy to cross; a raging flood is not; "ending birth and death is not so easy."
The six floods are the six senses: "the flood of the eye, by which forms are seen", and so on to the mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: senses, consciousness, and objects interact unbroken, "like a waterfall".

**Bodily ease**: the trainee, through mindfulness, no longer dwells in craving or aversion towards forms. **Mind well liberated**: the latent tendencies of the five lower fetters are cut; this is the non-returner, who has crossed the five floods.

The sixth flood, the mind, is crossed through **no contrivance** (無作, no wish even for the peak of existence), **no movement** (不傾動, untouched by pride, no delight in absorption), and **sustained mindfulness** (the four foundations within concentration). Venerable Miào Jìng: "In nirvāṇa all beings are equal; who is higher than whom?"

"No movement" may also mean the wholesome root of **loving-kindness**, free of hatred: calm through loving-kindness, insight through mindfulness. Master Cháng Bǎi: Dharma-based loving-kindness does not cling to oneself as the one who is kind.

quiz.q: From which five causes does the treatise say craving-desire arises?
options: perceiving as pure and lovely, delight in it, conceiving a being, intense craving, and latent tendency not yet exhausted
quiz.why: "First, from perceiving something as pure and lovely; second, from delight taken in that perception; third, from conceiving of a being as such; fourth, from craving already intensely habituated; and fifth, from the latent tendency not yet entirely exhausted." They run from coarse to subtle.

quiz.q: Before the signless concentration is perfected, what problem remains for stream-enterers through non-returners, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: they already sense non-self, but pride remains — "you don't practice, I do"
they may still fall into the lower realms
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a stream-enterer practising the four foundations already senses non-self, but pride remains — "you haven't practised, I have" — that lofty mind is still there. Hence the signless must be cultivated to sever the pride of the path of cultivation.

quiz.q: What two kinds of stillness does the treatise name, and which causes accomplish each?
options: bodily and mental, two causes each
stillness of present manifestation, by the first four causes; permanent severance of the latent tendency, never to arise again, by the fifth alone
with and without remainder, five causes each
worldly and transcendent, both by the first cause
quiz.why: "First, stillness of present manifestation; and second, the permanent severance of the latent tendency, such that it never arises again in future. The first four causes accomplish the first kind of stillness; the fifth cause alone accomplishes the second."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi define a "seed"?
options: the capacity that can produce phenomena is called a seed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is called a seed? The functional capacity that can produce phenomena is called a seed. The latent tendency is the seed of affliction; only the fifth cause, extinguishing it, achieves the second kind of stillness.

quiz.q: Why, per Venerable Miào Jìng, is the image of a "raging flood" used?
options: a slow current is weak and easy to cross; a raging flood is hard — ending birth and death is not easy
the Buddha lived by a river
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a slow current has no force and is easy to cross; a raging flood is hard to cross — that is, ending birth and death is not so easy. He adds that greed, hatred, and delusion flowing out as the eye faculty gives rise to eye consciousness is the flood.

quiz.q: The treatise says there are six floods. What are they?
options: the eye flood by which forms are seen, through to the mind flood by which mental objects are cognized — the activity of the six faculties
quiz.why: "There are six floods: the flood of the eye, by which forms are seen, and so on through to the flood of the mind, by which mental objects are cognized." Master Cháng Bǎi: the six faculties, consciousnesses, and objects interact from morning to night, from birth to death, unbroken like a waterfall.

quiz.q: Under the second explanation, what is "no movement," and how does it relate to calm and insight?
options: the wholesome root of loving-kindness, free of hatred by nature; calm-abiding through loving-kindness, insight through the foundations of mindfulness
meditation, unrelated to calm and insight
quiz.why: "'No movement,' under a second explanation, is the wholesome root of loving-kindness, being by nature free of hatred." "Calm-abiding through loving-kindness, insight through the foundations of mindfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on Dharma-based loving-kindness, one does not cling to oneself as the one showing compassion or the other as its object.
